newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi sees 96 profit up 10 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi sees 96 profit up 10 pct - paper.

text.p: French pharmaceuticals and beauty products company Sanofi chairman Jean-Francois Dehecq reaffirmed in an interview with the newspaper Le Figaro that the company's 1996 profit should rise 10 percent.
Asked whether the 1996 net profit would match initial forecasts of a rise of about 10 percent, he answered, "Yes, the results will conform to forecasts."
He said the beauty products division posted a "good second half, given the (economic) situation, after an unfavourable first half."
In 1995, the pharmaceutical unit of oil company Elf recorded net attributable profit of 1.58 billion francs, up 18.6 percent over the previous year.
Elf announced last month that it wanted Sanofi to find a merger partner to boost its profitability but said then that no talks were under way.
Dehecq said Elf's announcement gave Sanofi "greater development potential. It will allow it, if an opportunity arises, to develop also by external growth as it has done for the past 20 years.
Dehecq said potential partners would "naturally have profiles that would complement Sanofi's".
